summary: Intermittent long boot delay after suspend/resume during post-provisioning checks on Dell Latitude fleet
description:
Issue summary:
Intermittent long (30s–3min) boot delays observed after suspend/resume sequences on newly provisioned Dell Latitude devices. Delay occurs during early post-resume boot stage where provisioning agent / device health checks run; affected devices sometimes fail SCCM/Intune post-provisioning tasks and require a manual hard power cycle to continue.

Impact:
- Blocks zero-touch provisioning verification for a subset of new hires (observed ~6% of imaged units in last two weeks).
- Increases depot turnaround time and escalations to IT depot team.

Observed behavior:
- Device wakes from S3, shows manufacturer logo, then stalls with backlight on but no progress for variable time (30s–180s).
- Event Viewer shows Kernel-Boot/ID 27 and Kernel-Power/ID 1 around the timestamps; Winlog contains repeated ACPI warnings and "RDRAND instruction stall" style messages on affected hosts.
- When the device finally continues, provisioning agent reports timeout for policy application and retries; some devices never complete and are reimaged.

When it started:
- First reports: 2026-03-01 after a mini-bios fleet rollout (vendor BIOS 1.7.4) and our updated base image (image build 2026-02-20). Correlated to BIOS + driver bundle change.

Scope:
- Primary repro on Dell Latitude 7440 and 9550 running Windows 11 22H2 corporate image. Identical symptoms on AC and battery. Not seen on older Latitude 7300 fleet or on macOS devices.

Steps to reproduce (lab):
1) Provision a test Dell Latitude 7440 with image build 2026-02-20 using SCCM autopilot flow.
2) Complete OOBE and device registers in Intune.
3) Put device to sleep via Win+X -> Sleep (S3).
4) Wake device after ~10s. Observe boot progress; note any long pause between manufacturer logo and Windows boot/resume activity.

Logs / artifacts collected:
- Full Windows Event Log export (EVTX) from two affected devices (attached to ticket).
- Kernel memory dump taken on one repro (s3_resume_kdump_7440_20260305.dmp).
- Series of serial-over-usb traces from vendor recovery console showing ACPI _PTS/_WAK transitions.
- SCCM/Intune agent logs showing policy timeout (PolicyAgent.log).

Workarounds attempted:
- Disable "Fast Startup" in Windows: reduces frequency but does not eliminate.
- Revert BIOS to prior vendor release 1.6.9 in lab: reproducibility dropped to ~1% (suggests BIOS regression).
- Updated chipset drivers to latest vendor package: no consistent effect.
- Temporary manual workaround for depot: instruct technicians to perform a power cycle after any resume stall in post-provisioning stage.
investigation_notes:
Reproduction: Lab image reproduced the stall reliably on 3/5 with BIOS 1.7.4; rollback to 1.6.9 made it rare. Kernel dump analysis (WinDbg) shows long delay in ACPI _PTS handler and spin in rdrand/entropy collection path that blocks scheduler on some cores. Hypothesis: BIOS change modifies ACPI _PTS/_Sx coordination which, combined with our driver stack change in 2026-02 image, exposes a timing deadlock when RNG/entropy instruction (RDRAND) is used by crypto library early in resume path.

Actions taken so far:
- Imaging team pinned image build 2026-02-20 in staging and reverted a non-essential driver update (openssl/crypto shim) to test interaction.
- Firmware team contacted vendor (Dell) and opened vendor case #DEL-2026-311 (reference included in Confluence page). Vendor acknowledgment: "we see ACPI timing changes in 1.7.4; providing debug BIOS build for testing."
- SRE reproduced the stall in a controlled rack and captured full serial logs and S3 transition traces.

Preliminary root-cause (working): Combination of BIOS 1.7.4 ACPI timing change + our updated crypto/PRNG initialization during system resume can spin-wait on CPU feature instruction under specific core scheduling leading to long resume delays. Not yet confirmed as single root cause, vendor debug BIOS pending.

Next steps:
- Test vendor debug BIOS build in lab (arrived 2026-03-14, testing in progress).
- If vendor BIOS fixes, plan rollout with staged canary (10% devices) + monitor resume-failure metric.
- If BIOS cannot be rolled quickly, prepare automated provisioning check to detect stall and force graceful power cycle and retry provisioning agent to avoid manual depot triage.
- Create imaging rollback (driver shim) patch if driver-only repro is confirmed.

resolution:
In Progress - no final fix applied yet. Current mitigations: (1) Depot technicians instructed to perform hard power-cycle on devices that stall during provisioning resume; (2) Imaging team prepared a patched staging image rollback (reverted crypto shim) for canary testing; (3) Vendor debug BIOS received and being validated in lab.

Planned resolution steps if vendor BIOS confirms fix:
- Coordinate staged firmware rollout with Hardware ops (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%).
- Update SCCM autopilot post-provisioning script to include a resume-detection timeout and automated retry/power-cycle to avoid manual triage.

If driver-only fix confirmed:
- Publish image patch and schedule canary rollout across regional depots.
